defects: Requires CompleteLinearOrder α instead of LinearOrder α, restricting the theorem to complete lattices and losing gold's generality (gold applies to any LinearOrder with OrderTopology, complete or not, e.g. ℚ)
Requires CompleteLinearOrder β instead of LinearOrder β, same unnecessary restriction on the codomain

Adds an extra hypothesis hbot : f ⊥ = ⊥ that is not part of the gold statement; this fact should follow from continuity+monotonicity (it's part of what LeftOrdContinuous implies at s = ∅), not be assumed as a premise
Uses OrderClosedTopology β instead of OrderTopology β, a different (weaker) topological hypothesis on β than gold's

Conclusion is reformulated as an unconditional sSup equality f (sSup s) = sSup (f '' s) for all sets s (relying on completeness so sSup is always defined), rather than gold's LeftOrdContinuous f, which via IsLUB only asserts the property for sets that actually possess a supremum — this changes the scope/generality of the claim, not just its packaging
